name: Solar PV Cost Modeler
tagline: Builds a component-level cost model for a utility-scale solar PV (and optional storage) project from editable inputs.
problem: Estimating what a solar plant should cost means stitching together module, inverter, storage, balance-of-system, labour, margin and O&M assumptions, usually in a fragile spreadsheet. This tool puts those inputs in one form, computes minimum sustainable price (MSP) and minimum market price (MMP) ranges per component, checks them against market benchmarks and explains each step. It is aimed at developers, analysts and students learning PV project economics.
how: The form loads default values from the backend and groups inputs by component: system, modules, inverters, storage, structural BOS, electrical BOS, labour, other costs and O&M.
You edit any field, switch between PV only and PV plus storage, and press Run Analysis.
The FastAPI orchestrator validates the inputs and the calculator computes MSP and MMP ranges in $/kWdc for every component and the system total.
A research agent compares inputs and outputs to market ranges and attaches cited benchmark sources such as NREL and BNEF reports.
A lecture agent builds a step-by-step explanation of each calculation, and an exporter can write the model to Excel.
features: Collapsible input sections for nine cost components with min and max ranges, using the backend's own field names and defaults
PV only and PV plus storage system types
Inverter type and racking (tracker or fixed tilt) selectors
MSP and MMP cost ranges per component, with the Excel-style formula used
Cost Results tab with summary cards, a component bar chart, an MSP distribution pie and detailed tables
System Diagram tab: interactive React Flow schematic of modules, inverters, electrical BOS and storage with per-node details
Educational Content tab: step-by-step lecture sequence with formulas, worked examples, cost breakdowns and context
Market Research tab: range checks of inputs and outputs against benchmarks, plus cited source excerpts and suggestions
Excel export of inputs, outputs and formulas
Session endpoints for saving and updating a model
ai: The backend is structured as agents (calculator, validation, web research, lecture, Excel export) coordinated by a MultiAgentOrchestrator.
In this repo the agents are deterministic Python: the research agent returns built-in market ranges and cited benchmark excerpts rather than live scraping, and no LLM is called at runtime.
A separate research orchestrator module sketches a RAG pipeline (query decomposition, hybrid BM25 and dense retrieval, reranking, evidence extraction, synthesis) but is not wired into the API.
LangChain, OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs are listed in requirements for planned use.

stack.frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Zustand, Recharts, React Flow, Framer Motion
stack.data: In-memory sessions; openpyxl and xlsxwriter for Excel export
stack.ai: Rule-based agent classes; LangChain/OpenAI/Anthropic listed but not called
stack.deploy: Frontend on Vercel, API on Render (per vercel.json rewrite)

screens.title: Configure solar system
screens.caption: The input screen with all fields populated from the backend defaults. A three-step guide shows the flow: configure, run analysis, view results.

screens.title: Inverters and storage
screens.caption: Inverter type and cost range, then the ESS section where System Type is switched to PV + Storage, with battery cost, incentive and efficiency.

screens.title: Balance of system and labour
screens.caption: Structural BOS (racking area, tracker and fixed costs), electrical BOS (transformers, breakers, combiners, wiring, shipping and tariff) and labour rates and hours.

screens.title: Other costs and O&M
screens.caption: Sales tax, contingency, management overhead and profit, then the O&M cost ranges and discount rate.

screens.title: Analysis complete
screens.caption: After Run Analysis the backend returns the model, a completion toast appears, a session id shows in the header and all result tabs unlock.

screens.title: Cost results
screens.caption: Total MSP and MMP in $/kWdc, system and AC size, a component cost bar chart and the MSP distribution including storage.

screens.title: Detailed cost tables
screens.caption: Min, max and median MSP and MMP per component with the system total and its formula, then the PV plus storage table.

screens.title: System diagram
screens.caption: Interactive schematic of modules, inverters, electrical BOS and storage with DC, AC and charge/discharge links. Clicking a node shows its cost and parameters.

screens.title: Educational content
screens.caption: Step 1 of the lecture sequence explains system size and ILR in plain language with the formula and a worked example.

screens.title: Lecture step on storage
screens.caption: The storage step shows the battery capacity formula, an example calculation, the cost breakdown and real-world context.

screens.title: Market research
screens.caption: Range check of the module cost input against market ranges, with cited NREL, BNEF and PVInsights excerpts.

screens.title: Research flagging an output
screens.caption: The O&M tab flags the computed O&M figure as outside the benchmark range, showing how output validation reports problems.

run:
cd backend && python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev
notes: Backend and frontend ran locally with no LLM keys; the research data and lecture text are built into the code. Fixes committed in the local repo (not pushed): a PostCSS config and the missing Tailwind colour tokens (nothing-*, grid-line, border, using the hex values in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); input forms rewritten to use the backend's field names so no field is blank; the store now edits inputs locally and sends them with /calculate; the Cost Results, System Diagram, Educational Content and Market Research views now read the real /calculate response (data, lecture_sequence, web_research) and were restyled for the light theme; the Excel export request and two backend export bugs were fixed; React Flow nodes no longer remount and show connection edges; the dev server port and API proxy target can be set with VITE_PORT and VITE_API_URL. All screens, including the previously uncapturable result tabs, are real captures of the fixed app with PV + Storage selected and otherwise default inputs. Caveats: the backend's calculator returns a very small inverter cost (about $0.04/kWdc) and the O&M output is flagged outside the benchmark range by the app's own research check; these are the backend's numbers and were not changed. The research agent returns built-in benchmark excerpts, not live web results. The research orchestrator RAG module is not wired into the API.
